records.claim: Remark 2.2(i) — usual stochastic order equivalence
records.quote: Remark 2.2 (i) The over-assessment and under-assessment of a reliability function (say SF, FR, RFR, MRL, AI) are basically the study of the stochastic ordering (respectively, usual stochastic order, FR order, RFR order, MRL order, AI order, respectively) among the corresponding function between the dependent and independent counterpart of the system concerned. Mathematically, we express as, let TD and TI represent the lifetime of the series system formed by n dependent and independent components respectively. Clearly, TD ≤ST (≥ST )TI if and only if there is OA (U A) in SF .
records.family: general — n dependent vs independent components

hypotheses.text: TD and TI are lifetimes of the series system formed by n dependent and n independent components

conclusion.direction: TD ≤ST (≥ST) TI iff OA (UA) in SF — definitional equivalence between SF error sign and the usual stochastic order

records.ambiguity: Printed as a numbered Remark asserting iff equivalences; kind normalized to 'theorem' (spec enum has no 'remark'). Applies to a fully general class, but the paper instantiates each named order for specific families in Section 3; Proposition 2.1 (agreed by both passes) is the analogous dependence-side bridge.
